blocks.content: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species is the world's most comprehensive inventory of the global conservation status of biological species.

items: Critically Endangered (CR) criteria require a population decline of ≥90% over 10 years or 3 generations when causes are reversible, or ≥80% when causes are not understood or ongoing.
In the IUCN Red Data Book, endangered species are traditionally printed on Pink Pages, whereas recovered species that are no longer endangered are moved to Green Pages.
Remember that 'Data Deficient' (DD) is not a threatened category; it signifies a need for more research before an assessment can be completed.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The IUCN Red List classifies species into nine precise categories based on extinction risk, ranging from Extinct (EX) to Least Concern (LC).
The three officially recognized 'Threatened' categories are Critically Endangered (CR), Endangered (EN), and Vulnerable (VU).
Classification relies on five quantitative criteria: population reduction rate, geographic range, small population size, restricted population, and quantitative analysis.
Species that exist only in captivity, cultivation, or outside their historic natural range are categorized as Extinct in the Wild (EW).
Taxa with insufficient information to make a direct or indirect assessment of risk are categorized as Data Deficient (DD).
